title: fix(update): avoid downloading unrelated Git history during checks
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Git availability checks downloading unrelated branch and tag histories, potentially consuming gigabytes, when a fresh SHA-only source installation has no local upstream ref yet. The Gateway's post-ready update check and `openclaw update status` share this path.

## User Impact

Checks refresh the selected upstream and preserve existing shallow boundaries, local refs and tags. Fresh detached Dev installations discover their upstream on the first check. Configured tracking wins; a matching saved receipt then preserves the intended upstream, including when its local cache ref must be restored. Only installations with neither configured tracking nor matching receipt intent infer the Dev default. Excluded, genuinely ambiguous or unresolvable receipt intent stays unknown instead of selecting another upstream.

This does not reclaim already-downloaded packs or impose a universal byte limit. Missing history belonging to the selected upstream may still be downloaded. Disconnected shallow histories remain unknown rather than being reported as ahead, behind or current.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the selected source before fetching instead of falling back to an implicit `fetch --prune`. Git continues to own configured destination and force rules; the command selects one source, passes through negative refspecs and disables tag/prune side effects. Fresh `FETCH_HEAD` evidence must agree with the selected upstream before reporting a refreshed comparison.

Saved update receipts store a destination, sometimes abbreviated, without its source binding. The existing receipt format also permits a missing local cache. Reverse lookup therefore uses configured mappings and negative refspecs. Materialized names remain Git-resolved; missing full names use Git's ref validator. Missing abbreviations use the documented [Git refname namespaces](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrevisions). Only spelling ambiguity on one configured remote can use one explicit `ls-remote --refs` query; local probes remain offline, and competing source bindings/remotes remain unknown. This preserves published receipt data without changing its format or guessing an alternative remote.

An initial implementation reconstructed force policy too; real Git experiments showed source-only fetch could leave that responsibility with Git, so that code was removed. Final production delta is +128 lines, justified by source selection and existing receipt spelling/freshness contracts; tests are +451 and docs +8. No updater lifecycle, service, schema, public configuration option or deployment changes.

## Evidence

- Real local `file://` Git remote through `checkUpdateStatus`: the original path grew object storage from **8 to 2,072 KiB**, imported an unrelated 2 MiB blob/branch/tag, and still lacked first-check upstream counts. The repaired path grew **8 to 12 KiB**, fetched only `origin/main`, excluded unrelated objects/tag, retained the shallow boundary, and reported **0 ahead / 1 behind**. These are fixture measurements, not a global disk bound.
- Initial 12-case regression against original production: **10 failed, 2 passed**. Review then caught receipt edge cases before landing: an excluded alias counted as ambiguous; inferred origin preempted a matching custom receipt; deleted full or abbreviated receipt refs could not be restored. Each has captured original-production PASS / earlier-candidate RED evidence and is corrected in this head.
- Final selected real-Git/status/startup suites: **173 tests passed**. Exact-head real-Git file: **23/23 passed**, **41.71s wall** with `--maxWorkers=1` (37.63s Vitest). Coverage includes custom mappings, non-force destinations, local upstreams, excluded and competing bindings, receipt priority, missing full/abbreviated refs, ref/tag and object preservation, first-check availability and disconnected shallow histories.
- Independent Codex reviews of supplied diff and owner context through P2: **no remaining actionable findings**. Reviewers did not execute or independently verify reported tests; maintainer source/dependency review and executed proof are separate evidence.
- Final complete changed gate passed, including all 25 core test type programs. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36042945506) passed in **16m46s** overall elapsed time. No fleet host was used for proof.

### Published updater → candidate receipt proof

**Passed on head `94934c58597f72e8a2395bbcef71fa572e007c8c`.** A checksum-verified published `openclaw@2026.9.6` Git CLI performed a genuine Git revision update with `--channel dev --yes --json --no-restart`. The existing native version-1, note-only notice context requested a sentinel; it supplied no session, run or requester authority. The updater created the run and persisted its own result. An owned candidate Gateway then consumed the receipt through `update.status` with `refreshCheckout: true`.

The cell reused the repository's package-derived Git fixture helpers. Their canonical build helper bound generated build metadata to the synthetic Git revision before Gateway startup; compiled runtime files remained identical to the candidate tree. Source commit, transport commit, package digest and synthetic installation revision are separate identities:

```text
Published driver: 2026.9.6, registry SHA512 verified
Candidate source: 94934c58597f72e8a2395bbcef71fa572e007c8c
Candidate source tree: 5131629a0f752c95ea2c8205f634f2b3343a3e27
Source-capsule carrier: cd54d3b05df0b4d8733d17262848211f02b7deb7
Candidate package SHA256: 9690f466ed6192a0e12bd707a1ef1c744d3abb5c3ffa8db385971c0375a0d7e5
Native update: ok / git
Before fixture SHA: a070c6d6a5717c897b069e060a65fbcebc3ca39c
After fixture SHA: 4436d73fa0592f6dd4c1b388954ea1773b152029
Saved upstream: upstream/main
Gateway comparison: behind 1; installedAtMs 1790278839267
Gateway process group: joined
```

The original `origin` mapping remained present and pointed to a distinct two-commits-ahead remote. Local `main`, `origin/main` and branch-main tracking metadata were absent before boot. Returning the custom upstream's one-commit comparison plus the persisted installation timestamp therefore exercised receipt-based selection. [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36048614073), native command exit **0**, lease `tbx_01m3aebnm8g2qv7ncj6nezsgts`; the cell used an owned foreground Gateway, without managed-service restart coverage.

Earlier successful standalone CLI updates did not request notices and consequently produced no receipt; those runs are not counted as this proof. One initial harness assertion also expected `before.sha` in a package-mode report; the native successful update was preserved and only remaining checks resumed. The final passing cell above uses the correct published Git producer and explicit notice intent.

ClawSweeper's requested published-driver/saved-receipt proof and Rank-up move are addressed by this result. Named follow-up: the pre-existing CLI `update status` caller does not hydrate saved receipts; this cell uses the actual Gateway receipt consumer, and CLI hydration is outside this repair.
